facts.statement: The genus Cardiocorax was first named by a team of researchers including Ricardo Araújo and Octávio Mateus in 2015.
facts.quote: Cardiocorax was first named by Ricardo Araújo, Michael J. Polcyn, Anne S. Schulp, Octávio Mateus, Louis L. Jacobs, A. Olímpio Gonçalves and M.-L. Morais in 2015

facts.statement: A complete skull and partial postcrania attributed to Cardiocorax were found by Octávio Mateus in 2017.
facts.quote: In 2017 Octávio Mateus found a complete skull and partial postcrania also attributed to Cardiocorax.

facts.statement: The genus name Cardiocorax refers to a unique heart-shaped opening between the shoulder bones.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Latinised Greek Kardia, meaning "heart", plus corax, meaning "raven/crow" which is also the source of the name "coracoid", in reference to the heart-shaped fenestra between the coracoids which is unique to this genus.

facts.statement: The species name mukulu means "ancestor" in Angolan Bantu dialects.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie proviene de la palabra mukulu de los dialectos del bantú angoleño, el cual significa "ancestro".

facts.statement: Cardiocorax is an extinct genus of elasmosaurid plesiosaur found in southern Angola.
facts.quote: Cardiocorax is an extinct genus of elasmosaurid known from the Late Cretaceous (early Maastrichtian stage) Mocuio Formation of Namibe Province, southern Angola.

facts.statement: Fossils of Cardiocorax date to the early Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 71.40 to 71.64 million years ago.
facts.quote: They were collected from the Mocuio Formation of the Sāo Nicolau Group of Namibe Basin, dating to the early Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, 71.40–71.64 million years ago.

facts.statement: The known specimens of Cardiocorax are housed at the Museu de Geologia da Universidade Agostinho Neto in Luanda.
facts.quote: Both specimens are housed at the Museu de Geologia da Universidade Agostinho Neto in Luanda.

facts.statement: Cardiocorax is a distinctive elasmosaurid possessing four unique traits known as autapomorphies.
facts.quote: Cardiocorax es un elasmosáurido relativamente distintivo, el cual posee cuatro rasgos únicos, conocidos como autapomorfias.

facts.statement: The time range for Cardiocorax is recorded as the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Cardiocorax possesses a reduced dorsal blade of the scapula, a trait unique among elasmosaurids but similar to related cryptoclidid plesiosaurs.
rejected.quote: Notably, it shows a reduced dorsal blade of the scapula, a feature unique among elasmosaurids, but convergent with the related cryptoclidid plesiosaurs.
